items.title: 68357_Jimmy Maxwell oral history interview
items.q: Frieda Price had this house with a lot of girls where I played.

ctx.x: A whorehouse down what they call south of the tracks. This was where Mexican families lived and the non-Anglo-Saxon families lived, on the south side. And this one street, I'm embarrassed to tell you the title, was called

King Nigger Alley.
(Laughter.)
And that's where the black prostitutes were and the classier ones lived down at the end of the street. Frieda Price had this house with a lot of girls where I played. And my father, as I told you earlier, was a gambler. And although he was born in Texas and raised in Missouri, he didn't give a damn what anybody was as long as they were gamblers. So he would often bring some guy down on his luck over to the house, he would be a black guy. If he was a bigtime gambler, he liked him.

One of my earliest recollections, when I was about four we lived two miles out of town and for some reason they were running this black guy out of town. In those days they literally ran you out of town. The sheriff sat on the fender with a shotgun and this poor black guy is running in front of the car. Now, if he runs off the road they shoot him and if he doesn't keep running, they run over him.
